heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings (two uniform 256-bit words each); their chaining values CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: for every fixed variant a0, Pr[W7x in F7] = p7 = 287,309,824/2^32 exactly, and given it (W0..W6) is uniform and independent of W7 (Lemma 5.1); E16x is uniform for a good pair, so a lane passes the 8 tested bits with probability 2^-8 and the row-16 set with probability 160/2^32; the expected numbers of passing classes (0.53516) and good pairs (13,152) per first block; independence across first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected counts per first block that fix the work (V_MAX), the law of the second-block words that defines q3, and the independence of the first blocks (proof.md Sections 5 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact distribution of the number of passing classes over all 2^32 values of A_{-1} for the 8 classes (p8hits.c, Appendix A.2); 29,360,128 (2^22 + 2^23 + 2^24) real first blocks through the attack's own filters with the 8 classes (proof.md Section 13.1, e2ep8.c): passing classes, good pairs and stage-3a passes within 0.07% of their expectations, 14,199 row-16 passes against 14,385.0 expected (z = -1.55), every one checked exactly in Python (the first block gives the chaining value, the variant is selected, rows -4..16 hold in both members); the organizer experiment a0-online-r38.
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on 2^24 first blocks, not 2^82. The class tests of one first block are correlated (at most 2 of the 8 classes pass); only the expectations and the exact probability that some class passes enter the ledger.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 196,608 selected variants (the 8 classes of mask 7fe96c7c) of Pr[the pair is in the accepted event: rows 16..21 of both members follow every cell, '+' pair and two-bit condition of P8 closing at rows 16..21, row 19 on its signed differences only, the relation E18 = E17 (bits 24, 23, 15) not imposed, and the state words A34..A37, E34..E37 of the two members are equal]; q3 >= q3_model = 2^-96.2901.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: The declared factor is the shipped replica's one-sided 99% lower bound for the printed-cell event (proof.md Section 7.4b and Appendix A.12; preregistered before the first seed, SHA-256 12cadbfa...): 2,000 fresh replicates of smc_replicate in 100 pools of 20, 0 failed rebuilds, L = -96.2499, pool sd 0.1699, declared one-sided 99% lower bound 2^-96.2901; every success is rebuilt into a verified 38-step semi-free-start collision and accepted by the counted program. The printed-cell event imposes E18 = E17 and the row-19 conditions; the accepted event imposes the same rows with row 19 on signed differences only and does not impose E18 = E17, so it contains the printed-cell event and q3_accepted >= q3_printed >= 2^-96.2901. No ratio is used. A fresh 2,000-replicate rerun of the same replica gives L = -96.2637, pool sd 0.1201, one-sided 99% lower bound 2^-96.2916, confirming the declared factor. Our 960-replicate calibration (mean 2^-96.3095) and 1a695f0b's estimator (mean 2^-96.3683) agree within 0.05 bit. The organizer experiment a0-q3-r38 runs the replica with a pass rule frozen before its calibration (pooled mean of 20 >= 2^-97.0).
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo lower bound from the shipped replica. The replica is a restricted lower bound: its row-19 proposals use 1a695f0b's twelve conditions, W23 in F23 and the characteristic's path from row 22, and it does not sample the extra successes of the relaxation (E18 different from E17); those successes are additional, so the bound is conservative. The 2,000 replicates are treated as 100 independent pools. The bound is one-sided 99%.

heuristics.statement: Let R_f be the number of selected variants of first block f that are good and pass row 16, and A_t the event that trial t = (f, a0) succeeds. Averaged over successes, the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times: sum_t Pr[A_t] E[R_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-7.5 E[X_f].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= E[X_f] - E[X_f (X_f - 1)]/2 >= (1 - 2^-8.5) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Under H1 the law of (CV1, a0) given a success is the law of the successes of the Step-3 sampler (proof.md Section 13.5). Our measurement on successes of the accepted event: 12,028 successes of 8 independent runs of the replica's sampler (all 8 classes, a0 uniform on the 196,608 variants), each rebuilt into a verified pair and accepted by step3b, every selected variant of every passing class of its chaining value tested: 32 other row-16 passes against 21.95 under independence, 2^-8.55 per success, one-sided 99% upper bounds 2^-7.97 (Poisson) and 2^-7.79 (Student over the 8 runs), below the premise; the stage-3a passes of the other variants are at 1.0008 of their expectation. 1a695f0b measured 2 other row-16 passes on 750 successes (quoted).
heuristics.limitations: The successes are sampled by the replica's sampler, a sub-event of the accepted event (row-19 relation sets, W23 in F23, zero differences from row 22), not real collisions; successes within a run share ancestors (the Student bound uses the 8 independent runs). The other row-16 passes exceed independence by a factor 1.46 (z = +2.15); the premise counts row-16 passes only, which is conservative. No organizer execution.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^56 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^56 is 12.4 bits above P8's own published search bound of 2^43.61 units; it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (57.58496).
heuristics.extrapolation: P8's search is published with its run log (1a695f0b Section 3.2, quoted; participant-run): 38 solver runs of at most 10,800 s (230,183 s in all), P8 found in 4,714 s with a 662-s coupling check; its author bounds the search, S, the class data and all development by one 10-core machine for less than 2^21 core-seconds, which at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second is 2^43.61 units, 12.4 bits under A_C = 2^56. Our own measurements of the same kind of search (proof.md Appendix C, from fb176310): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units, 16.85 bits under A_C. A_C = 2^56 leaves at least 12.4 bits over P8's own search for unrecorded failed and repeated runs; it replaces fb176310's inherited 2^78.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance, not our measurement: we did not rerun P8's search; its log and the 2^21 core-second bound are the author's. Its workspace is not part of this package's memory (Section 14). With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 86.06826.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) and the 8 class descriptors with their product description are obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^56 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^56, well below 0.001% of T); it is more than 20 bits above the 662-s coupling check.
heuristics.extrapolation: 1a695f0b obtained the pair in its 662-s coupling check and the class descriptors by 32 passes over a hash of c7 (quoted); our exhaustive pass over all 2^32 values of a0 (p8fam.c, 102 s, 69 MB peak) reproduces the 8 classes and their 24,576 members each, and selftest checks the product description. A_S = 2^56 is more than 20 bits above the 662-s coupling check and replaces fb176310's inherited 2^74.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance: the pair search was run by 1a695f0b, not by us; its time is charged as A_S and its workspace is not part of this package's memory (Section 14, r37 precedent 9c6967cc).

heuristics.statement: All development of this package (exhaustive passes, end-to-end runs, the q3 runs, the replica's development and calibration, the H3 measurement, the program scans and the cloud checks of the hoisted programs; failed trials and reruns included) is at most DEV = 2^56 target compressions. H4c is a time charge; the memory figure is H6.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^56, well below 0.001% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: Recorded development below 1.5 x 10^5 CPU-seconds (proof.md Section 13.4); at 10^10 word operations per CPU-second that is below 2^51 operations = 2^39.3 compressions, so 2^56 is more than 2^16 times the recorded work. Every development execution whose output the claim uses ran under a hard address-space cap of 2^27 or 2^28 bytes with its peak measured by memmeter; the largest peak is the development emulation at 2^26.35 bytes (proof.md Section 14 (c2), Appendix A.10).
heuristics.limitations: Accounting of our own runs, not an organizer log; declared here because the review of fb176310 recorded it as an implicit heuristic (H-implicit-development-bound). There are no other development executions in this construction.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, a straight-line word-RAM program that evaluates E16x = C16 + W0 + s0(W1) and its stage-3a test for 256 variants at once (bit L of every 256-bit word belongs to variant L) is charged its instruction list: every load, store and spill is counted, 64 registers, complements are free except in a mixed and/or (one more operation), no fused AND-NOT; one stage-2 program per batch, with the batch's constant bits of a0 folded into it, and one stage-1 program per (class, G1) whose stored planes the 32 stage-2 programs of its y values load (each store and each load is an instruction and is counted); no target compression is evaluated this way.
heuristics.scope: The plane-program term of the ledger (37,290.96 of the 43,396.40 data-dependent operations per first block).
heuristics.extrapolation: The 24 stage-1 and 768 stage-2 programs are generated and counted by experiments/a0hoist38.py (build_e16, group, Prog.schedule, run_prog): 574 to 579 instructions per stage-1 program and 681 to 725 per stage-2 program (mean 701.65), spills of at most 10 slots; every stage-2 program is executed with its stage-1 program by the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 on all its 256 lanes and compared with the scalar definition (196,608 lanes per request in the local emulation, 0 mismatches), as are the batches of the passing classes of its trials 0..5 and 6 sampled batches in selftest; on the cloud 23,592,960 lanes of 120 random chaining values, 0 mismatches.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited; the same reading was accepted for fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2. Program generation is charged 2^32 operations per program, not counted instruction by instruction. With a scalar evaluation (38 operations per variant) the claim would be 89.42650.

heuristics.statement: The peak memory is the maximum over the computations this package executes, <= 2^26.35 bytes (claim memory_log2_bytes = 26.35). The counted phases are the online program (17,734,944 bytes = 2^24.08), the joint verification of the published dense rows of S (33,212 KB = 2^25.02), the class descriptors (37,036 KB = 2^25.14), the class/program generation (64,484 KB = 2^25.98), the q3 replica (18,800 KB = 2^24.2) and the development emulation (83,568 KB = 2^26.35). The published searches of P8 and S are not executed by this package; they are charged in time as A_C = 2^56 and A_S = 2^56 (preprocessing 2^57.58496), following the r37 filing 9c6967cc (paired review plausible_not_refuted, memory 19.62, preprocessing 2^60.00141).
heuristics.scope: The memory metric of the claim and the score 85.67528 + (26.35 - 20) = 92.02528.
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 14 lists every online component and every executed stage with its measured peak: online 2^24.08; joint verification build 2^25.02 and solve 2^24.28; class descriptors 2^25.14; class/program generation 2^25.98; q3 replica 2^24.2; development emulation 2^26.35; organizer experiments within the 128 MiB sandbox. The published searches' peaks (Step-1 2^28.094 and signed search 2^27.92, measured by 1a695f0b) are not part of this package's execution; their time is charged as A_C/A_S.
heuristics.limitations: The published searches are cited, not re-run; their workspaces are excluded from memory because they are not executed by this package, following the r37 precedent 9c6967cc. The largest counted peak is our development emulation at 2^26.35; the machine model defines no code size (32 bytes per instruction is the generous choice).

heuristics.statement: In the hoisting step, two Boolean DAG nodes of the 32 batch programs with equal 512-bit evaluation signatures compute the same function (no false equivalence), so merging them leaves the generated program equal to the unhoisted one.
heuristics.scope: The node merging of the hoisted plane program (proof.md Section 9, hoisting): whether the generated program computes the reference row-16 filter. The counted operations are those of the generated program as written, exact whatever it computes; a false merge could only change which pairs pass the filter, hence the success probability, and every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory. The generated program agrees bit for bit with the reference on 23,592,960 cloud lanes (0 disagreements) and the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 (196,608 lanes, 0 mismatches); a false merge would change outputs on a positive fraction of inputs.
heuristics.limitations: Our theory, not a theorem: equal 512-bit evaluation signatures are taken to mean equal functions. Checked on 23,592,960 cloud lanes and the organizer's 196,608 lanes with 0 disagreements, not on all inputs.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is a verified collision of the target (Lemma 6.1, proof.md Section 6.1).

Algorithm: the two-block attack of ePrint 2026/1120 with the characteristic P8 of dariolina's 1a695f0b (its cells, its semi-free-start pair and the Step-1 solution S; member x = M) and the A0-variant method of fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2: 8 classes of 24,576 variants (mask 7fe96c7c, 1a695f0b's selection); one W7 test decides a class, every variant of a passing class is a good pair; per class and G1 a stage-1 plane program computes once the planes that do not depend on the 32 high-bit values y, and 768 straight-line stage-2 batch programs (the batch's constant bits of a0 folded) load them and evaluate E16x for 256 variants and test the 8 lowest bits shared by the 160 row-16 words; passing lanes resolved in scalar form; a row-16 pass is checked through row 21 (row 19 on its signed differences only, the relation E18 = E17 not imposed); rows 22..37 are computed untested and the output words of both members compared (proof.md Section 6.1).

Cost: fixed caps. N_FB = 3,650,944,274,160,560,947,189,532 first blocks (2^81.59454), each one target compression plus 35 counted operations, and V_MAX = 158,440,245,784,936,605,369,509,038,543 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded, tested at the start of every first block and after every class; at most V_MAX + 72,644,196, proof.md Lemma 8.1); allowances A_C = 2^56, A_S = 2^56 and the development charge DEV = 2^56 (H4a, H4b, H4c); counted precomputation 2^42.607 operations; final verification. Counted program: experiments/a0hoist38.py (24 stage-1 programs of 574 to 579 instructions, 768 stage-2 programs of 681 to 725 instructions, 2,825 operations for a row-16 pass). Exact total 2^85.6752734640 (proof.md Section 11, Appendix B), claimed 85.67528.

Success probability at least 0.39 (the bound is exactly 0.39) under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-96.2901 for the accepted event of proof.md Section 6.1: the shipped replica's one-sided 99% lower bound of the printed-cell event over the 196,608 selected variants, 2,000 fresh replicates, L = -96.2499, pool sd 0.1699, proof.md Section 7.4b and Appendix A.12; the printed-cell event imposes E18 = E17 and is a sub-event of the accepted event, which does not impose it, so the same bound holds for the accepted event; no ratio is used) and H3 (averaged over successes, the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times; measured 2^-8.55), by Bonferroni per first block, independence across first blocks and Chebyshev for the work cap; a cap halt happens only if the total work exceeds V_MAX, probability at most P_cap 8.540e-31, inside the bound (proof.md Section 10). No expected-work bound is used.

Memory: peak 2^26.35 bytes = maximum over the computations this package executes: online 17,734,944 bytes (2^24.08); the joint verification of the published dense rows of S 33,212 KB (2^25.02); the class descriptors 37,036 KB (2^25.14); the class/program generation 64,484 KB (2^25.98); the q3 replica 18,800 KB (2^24.2); the development emulation 83,568 KB (2^26.35). The published characteristic search and Step-1 search of 1a695f0b are not executed by this package; they are charged in time as A_C = 2^56 and A_S = 2^56 (preprocessing 2^57.58496), following the accounting of our r37 filing 9c6967cc (paired review plausible_not_refuted, memoryLog2Bytes 19.62, preprocessingLog2 60.00141). H6. Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 85.67528 + 6.35 = 92.02528. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.
